title: Import a fleet
subtitle: Bring an existing Coolify instance into Tugra — its apps, domains and config. Nothing on the source is changed.
sourceCoolifyHint: Connect with a Coolify API token to preview everything it is running.
localDockerHint: Adopting plain Docker containers instead? Use "Discover" on a server's page.
tokenHint: Create the token on your admin/owner team with the read ability (add read:sensitive too — it's used at apply time to fetch env values). A 403 means Coolify's API "Allowed IPs" setting is on and doesn't include this hub's IP; add it there or clear the list.
targetHint: Where the imported apps and database records are created. Database DATA is moved by the separate migrator step; app volume data is copied manually.
noTarget: Add a server to this team first, then come back to import.
rollbackBody: Removes the apps this import created on the target server. Apps you have deployed since are kept. This cannot be undone.
migrateDesc: Your databases were recreated empty. Generate a one-time command and run it on your source (Coolify) host to copy each database's data into its new Tugra database. The token works once and expires.
migrateTokenOnce: Copy this now — the token is shown only once.
migrateActive: A migration command is active until {date}.
remapTitle: Point apps at their new databases
remapDesc: Rewrite each migrated app's environment so it connects to its new Tugra database instead of the old Coolify one. Preview the exact (secret-masked) changes first, then apply — changes take effect on each app's next deploy, and an undo is available.
remapNoLink: Won't auto-link the database network ({reason}) — wire it by hand
remapApplyBody: Rewrites the shown environment keys on each app. Changes take effect on the next deploy and can be undone.
remapApplied: Environment rewritten — redeploy each app to apply
